S: Smoked salmon blini and prosciutto figs
the last pair of black cashmere gloves

Blini with smoked salmon, crème fraîche and dill, plus figs wrapped in prosciutto with blue cheese, laid out on black slate. Warm 16 cocktail blini at 180C for 4 minutes. Top each with a spoon of crème fraîche, a curl of smoked salmon, a sprig of dill and a crack of pepper. Quarter 6 fresh figs, press a small piece of blue cheese into each, then wrap with a strip of prosciutto. Drizzle the figs with 1 tbsp honey and serve both on a dark board.
Molasses gingerbread spiced with ginger, cinnamon and cloves, baked in a tray at 170C, cut into squares with a lemon glaze.
Score chestnuts with a cross, soak 20 minutes, roast at 220C for 20 minutes until the shells curl, wrap in a towel 5 minutes, peel warm.
M: the dinner they could have had years earlier
Sirloin seared and basted with butter and thyme, rested, peppercorn sauce of brandy, stock and cream, double-fried frites.
Waldorf club sandwich with Waldorf salad
the lift ride test at the Waldorf

Triple-decker of roast chicken, crisp bacon, lettuce, tomato and mayo, pinned and cut, served with a Waldorf salad of apple, celery, grapes and walnuts. Grill 8 bacon rashers until crisp. Toast 12 slices white sandwich bread. Spread with mayo and build each sandwich as toast, 100g sliced roast chicken, lettuce, toast, 2 bacon rashers, sliced tomato, toast. Pin with skewers and cut into four triangles. For the salad, toss 2 diced red apples, 2 sliced celery sticks, 150g halved grapes and 60g toasted walnuts with 3 tbsp mayo and a squeeze of lemon.
W: Melt 100g dark chocolate with 2 tbsp cocoa, 2 tbsp sugar and 100ml milk, cool. Blend with 250ml milk and 3 cups of ice until slushy. Whipped cream and shaved chocolate.
K: the Waldorf elevators on a winter night
Cranberry juice warmed with orange slices, cinnamon and cloves, served hot in mugs.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170C and line a 20cm square tin. Melt the butter with the brown sugar and golden syrup.
Stir into the flour, bicarb, ginger and cinnamon with the egg and milk. Pour into the tin.
Bake until firm.
Cool in the tin.
Mix the icing sugar with the lemon juice, glaze the top and cut into squares.
Score a cross through the shell of each chestnut.
Soak in water and drain.
Roast on a tray at 220C until the shells curl back.
Wrap in a clean towel to steam.
Peel while still warm, sprinkle with salt and serve.
Cut the potatoes into thin frites, rinse and dry thoroughly.
Fry in 140C oil until cooked but pale, drain and cool.
While the frites cool, season the steaks.
Fry the frites again at 185C until crisp. Season with salt.
Sear the steaks in a heavy hot pan with oil on both sides.
Lower the heat, add the butter and thyme and baste briefly, then rest the steaks.
Add the peppercorns to the pan, then the brandy, carefully and away from the flame, and simmer briefly.
Add the stock and reduce, then stir in the cream and simmer. Serve with the steaks and frites.
Gently melt the chocolate with the cocoa, sugar and part of the milk, stirring until smooth.
Cool completely.
Blend with the rest of the milk and the ice until slushy.
Divide into small glasses, spoon over softly whipped cream and finish with shaved chocolate.
Warm the juice with one sliced orange, the cinnamon and cloves over low heat without boiling.
Strain into mugs and float a fresh orange slice on top of each.

s.note: Soft spiced gingerbread squares with a lemon glaze.
s.how: Melt 125g butter with 100g brown sugar and 150g golden syrup. Stir into 250g flour, 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda, 2 tsp ground ginger and 1 tsp cinnamon with 1 egg and 125ml milk. Bake in a lined 20cm square tin at 170C for 35 minutes, cool, glaze with 100g icing sugar and lemon juice and cut into 16 squares.

s.note: Warm roasted chestnuts peeled from their curled shells with flaky salt.
s.how: Score a cross through the shell of each of 400g chestnuts. Soak in water for 20 minutes and drain. Roast on a tray at 220°C conventional for 20 minutes until the shells curl back. Wrap in a clean towel for 5 minutes, then peel while still warm. Sprinkle with 1/4 tsp sea salt flakes and serve.

m.note: Butter basted sirloin, creamy brandy peppercorn sauce and double fried frites.
m.how: Cut 800g potatoes into thin frites, rinse and dry thoroughly. Fry in neutral oil at 140°C for 5 minutes, drain and cool 15 minutes, then fry again at 185°C for 3 minutes until crisp. Season with salt. Season four 200g sirloin steaks and sear in a heavy hot pan with 1 tbsp neutral oil for about 3 minutes each side. Lower the heat, add 40g butter and 4 thyme sprigs, baste for 1 minute, then rest the steaks 8 minutes. Add 1 tsp cracked black peppercorns to the pan. Carefully add 40ml brandy away from the flame and simmer 1 minute. Add 150ml beef stock, reduce 5 minutes, stir in 100ml thickened cream and simmer 3 minutes. Serve with steaks and frites.
shop: neutral oil for frying and searing@Pantry

w.note: Chocolate milk blended with ice, whipped cream and shaved chocolate.
w.how: Gently melt 100g dark chocolate with 2 tbsp cocoa powder, 2 tbsp caster sugar and 100ml full cream milk, stirring until smooth. Cool completely. Blend with another 250ml full cream milk and 3 cups of ice, about 450g, until slushy. Divide into four small glasses. Softly whip 100ml thickened cream, spoon on top and finish with 20g shaved dark chocolate.

d.note: Hot cranberry punch with orange, cinnamon and cloves.
d.how: Warm 1L cranberry juice with 1 sliced orange, 2 cinnamon sticks and 6 cloves over low heat for 15 minutes without boiling. Strain into 4 mugs and float a fresh orange slice on top of each.
